# Textarea

A labelled multi-line text input.

```tsx
import { Textarea } from "@rata/react";
```

| | |
|---|---|
| Registry name | `textarea` |
| Family | inputs |
| Tier | free |
| Status (css / react / figma) | latest / latest / future |
| Depends on | `field` |

## Behavior

A `<textarea>` inside a `Field`. No primitive of its own: `getFieldProps` already supplies every id and ARIA attribute, and a multi-line control needs nothing a single-line one does not.

- **A separate component, not a `multiline` prop on TextField** — `TextField` is typed to `HTMLInputElement` and forwards its ref as one, so a boolean that silently swapped the element would invalidate half its props at runtime while still compiling. The elements also differ in ways a caller has to know about: `rows` and `wrap` exist on one and not the other, and Enter inserts a newline here where it submits there. This system's test for splitting is a difference in semantics rather than in looks, and that is what this is — the same test that separated Text from Heading.
- **`rows` sets the height, and there is no `size` prop** — `TextField`'s `size` exists to choose a control height from the control scale. A multi-line control's height is how many lines it shows, which is what `rows` already says — offering both would be two props for one measurement, and a caller would have to guess which wins.
- **It does not grow with its content in this version** — The honest options are all costly: `field-sizing: content` is not supported widely enough to be the only mechanism, the replicated-content grid trick needs a wrapper element around the control that exists purely to be measured, and measuring in JS means a resize observer per field. Each is a real decision about the DOM this component puts on the page, and none of them should ride along with the box. `rows` plus a resize handle covers the case meanwhile, and the caller can see how much room they are giving.
- **`resize` defaults to `vertical`, and horizontal is not offered** — Letting a reader make the box taller is the cheapest possible fix for a field that turned out too small, and it costs the layout nothing — the control's inline size is the form's. Horizontal resize does cost the layout: a control dragged wider than its column overflows whatever contains it, and no form anticipates that. `none` is there for the layouts that cannot tolerate a height change either.
- **No character counter** — A counter is two things — a number that updates, and an announcement policy for when it should interrupt a typist — and both belong to the caller who knows the limit. `Field` already has the slot: `description` for the limit stated up front, `message` with `status="invalid"` for having passed it. Building it in would mean choosing a live-region policy on everyone's behalf.
- **`disabled` is `aria-disabled` plus `readOnly`, inherited from Field** — Nothing new is decided here; it is named so the contract does not read as though the question were open. The same consequence applies — a readOnly control still submits its value.

## Props

Extends `Omit<`.

| Prop | Type | Default | Summary |
|---|---|---|---|
| `label` | `ReactNode` | — | The control's label. Always required — `labelHidden` hides it, nothing removes it. |
| `rows?` | `number` | `3` | How many lines of text the control shows before it scrolls. |
| `resize?` | `TextareaResize` | `"vertical"` | Whether the reader may drag the control taller. |
| `labelHidden?` | `boolean` | — | Takes the label off screen while leaving it in the accessibility tree. |
| `id?` | `string` | — | Stable id for the control, when something outside needs to point at it. |
| `status?` | `FieldStatus` | `"idle"` | Validation lifecycle, driving the message tone, `aria-invalid`, `aria-busy` and the ring. |
| `description?` | `ReactNode` | — | Persistent helper text under the control. |
| `message?` | `ReactNode` | — | Status-dependent message under the control. |
| `required?` | `boolean` | — | Marks the control required, in the label and to assistive technology. |
| `disabled?` | `boolean` | — | Blocks editing while keeping the control focusable, readable and announced. |
| `className?` | `string` | — | Class for the wrapper — the width the form wants, not a restyle. |

### `label`

```ts
label: ReactNode
```

The control's label. Always required — `labelHidden` hides it, nothing removes it.

**Use when**

- A short noun phrase naming what goes in it: "Release notes", not "Type your release notes".

**Don't use for**

- Leaving it off because a placeholder says the same thing. The placeholder is gone on the first keystroke.

**Accessibility** Bound to the control by Field, so it is the accessible name and clicking it focuses the control.

### `rows`

```ts
rows?: number = 3
```

How many lines of text the control shows before it scrolls.

**Use when**

- Three for a note, eight or more for something someone will draft in.
- A number that matches what you expect, so the reader can see how much is wanted of them.

**Don't use for**

- One. A single-line control is a `TextField`, and a one-row textarea is that with worse keyboard behaviour — Enter inserts a newline instead of submitting.

### `resize`

```ts
resize?: TextareaResize = "vertical"
```

Whether the reader may drag the control taller.

**Use when**

- `none` only where a taller control would break the layout around it — a fixed-height panel, a row in a dense table.

**Don't use for**

- `none` as a default because the handle looks untidy. It is the cheapest fix a reader has for a field that turned out too small, and taking it away costs them more than it saves you.

### `labelHidden`

```ts
labelHidden?: boolean
```

Takes the label off screen while leaving it in the accessibility tree.

**Use when**

- A control whose meaning is already carried by a heading directly above it.

**Don't use for**

- Pairing it with a placeholder standing in for the name.

**Accessibility** The label element is still rendered and still bound. Only the pixels go.

### `id`

```ts
id?: string
```

Stable id for the control, when something outside needs to point at it.

Source doc: Stable id for the control. Defaults to a generated one.

**Use when**

- A form library that addresses fields by id, or an error summary linking to the control it names.

**Don't use for**

- Reusing one across two fields. Every id under it is derived from this.

### `status`

```ts
status?: FieldStatus = "idle"
```

Validation lifecycle, driving the message tone, `aria-invalid`, `aria-busy` and the ring.

Source doc: Validation lifecycle. Drives `aria-invalid`, `aria-busy`, and the ring.

**Use when**

- `invalid` with a `message` saying what to do about it.

**Don't use for**

- `invalid` with no message. The ring says something is wrong; only the message says what.

**Accessibility** Field's, unchanged: `invalid` sets `aria-invalid` and pulls the message into `aria-describedby`, and while idle the message stays on the page but leaves the chain.

### `description`

```ts
description?: ReactNode
```

Persistent helper text under the control.

**Use when**

- The length limit, stated before someone writes past it — this is where a counter's job mostly lives.

**Don't use for**

- Repeating the label in a sentence. It is read out after the name.

**Accessibility** Joins `aria-describedby` ahead of the message, so a constraint is heard before a failure.

### `message`

```ts
message?: ReactNode
```

Status-dependent message under the control.

**Use when**

- What to do about an `invalid` status, in the imperative: "Keep this under 500 characters."

**Don't use for**

- Putting the permanent limit here. It leaves the description chain whenever the status returns to idle — that is `description`.

**Accessibility** Announced politely rather than as an alert, because it is already in `aria-describedby`.

### `required`

```ts
required?: boolean
```

Marks the control required, in the label and to assistive technology.

Source doc: Marks the control required to assistive technology and in the label.

**Use when**

- Controls that genuinely block submission.

**Don't use for**

- Pairing it with a hand-written asterisk in `label`. Field renders one.

**Accessibility** `aria-required` on the control; the rendered marker is `aria-hidden`.

### `disabled`

```ts
disabled?: boolean
```

Blocks editing while keeping the control focusable, readable and announced.

**Use when**

- A note whose content is decided elsewhere and should still be readable in full.

**Don't use for**

- Assuming the value is withheld. `readOnly` still submits.

**Accessibility** `aria-disabled` plus `readOnly` from Field, never the native attribute.

### `className`

```ts
className?: string
```

Class for the wrapper — the width the form wants, not a restyle.

Source doc: Class for the wrapper. The control itself is styled by the system.

**Use when**

- The measure or grid placement the form decides.

**Don't use for**

- Setting a height. That is `rows`, and a hand-written height stops matching the line count the reader sees.

## Use cases

### A note someone will actually draft in

The commonest case: free text with a stated limit.

```tsx
<Textarea
  label="Release notes"
  rows={8}
  description="Markdown is fine. Around 500 characters reads best."
/>
```

The limit goes in `description` rather than a counter, because it is the thing worth knowing BEFORE writing. Eight rows says how much is wanted more honestly than any sentence would.

### Too long, and said so

Reporting a limit the writer has passed.

```tsx
<Textarea
  label="Release notes"
  status="invalid"
  message="Keep this under 500 characters."
/>
```

The message is the imperative, not the diagnosis — "too long" tells someone what happened, this tells them what to do. The ring and the colour say it twice more.

### A layout that cannot take a taller control

A fixed-height panel, or a control inside a dense row.

```tsx
<Textarea label="Internal note" rows={2} resize="none" labelHidden />
```

`none` because the container genuinely cannot grow, which is the only reason for it. The label is hidden rather than absent — the row's own header is carrying the name visually, and nothing about the accessible name changes.

### Reaching for the wrong component

The value is one line and Enter should submit the form.

```tsx
<Textarea label="Email" rows={1} />
```

Don't. That is `TextField`. A one-row textarea looks almost right and behaves wrong: Enter inserts a newline instead of submitting, and the value can arrive with line breaks in it that nothing upstream expects.

## Real usage in this repo

```tsx
<Textarea label="Internal note" rows={2} resize="none" labelHidden />
```

## Token recipe

### base

The box, and only the box — Field owns the label, helper text, message and disabled dimming. Every value below is the one `.rata-text-field-input` uses, deliberately: the two controls sit in the same form and a reader should not be able to tell they were built separately.

| Property | Token |
|---|---|
| font-family | `font.family.sans — a control inherits neither family nor size from the page, so both are stated` |
| font-size | `type.control.size.md — the same constant the button family and the text field use, so all three measure their text alike` |
| line-height | `type.control.line-height.md — and here it also decides the height, since `rows` multiplies it` |
| background | `theme.bg.surface` |
| color | `theme.fg.primary` |
| border-color | `theme.border.strong` |
| border-radius | `radius.element` |
| padding-inline | `space.control.padding-inline.md — matching the text field's md step, which is the only step this control has` |
| padding-block | `space.padding.xs — a single-line control centres its text with its height, and a multi-line one has no height to centre against, so the space has to be stated` |
| placeholder color | `theme.fg.muted` |

### states

Selected from the primitive's data-status on the Field root, exactly as the text field's are. The rings are inset strokes, never the focus ring, so a control can be focused and invalid at once.

| Property | Token |
|---|---|
| hover inner band | `theme.bg.muted at border.2 as an inset shadow, idle only — the validation rings occupy the same 2px and box-shadow does not accumulate` |
| focus border-color | `theme.fg.primary` |
| focus outline | `focus.ring-width solid theme.fg.primary at space.0 offset — the same deliberate departure the text field documents, so the two controls' focus looks identical` |
| validating ring | `theme.accent-role.ring` |
| valid ring | `theme.success-role.ring` |
| invalid ring | `theme.danger-role.ring` |
| disabled cursor | `not-allowed — the dimming itself is Field's, on the root` |
